audit.whatIsWrong: The two layers gave opposite level charts. Full read LeBlanc/LeBlanc/LeBlanc/LeBlanc/Skill/Skill/Skill; content read Cassiopeia x4 / LeBlanc / Cassiopeia / Cassiopeia. The packet flags its own chart: 'level chart contradicts data: Cassiopeia wins only 47.35% but the chart gives Cassiopeia 6/7 stages'. On top of that, all seven full-layer whys described Cassiopeia winning the stage while the side said LeBlanc.
audit.why: Resolvable from the kit, so I did not leave it alone: Sigil of Malice is a 700-range point-and-click on 6s against a delayed 850 zone; Distortion at 2 lets her leave before poison finishes; the Q-W-E chain at 3 is a full burst rotation against a Cassiopeia with no stun until 6; Mimic at 6 is her single biggest spike. Items are where Cassiopeia's sustained damage catches up, but LeBlanc still chooses when fights start — that is a genuine skill row, not a Cassiopeia row.
audit.corrected: Settled chart: LeBlanc, LeBlanc, LeBlanc, LeBlanc, LeBlanc, Skill, Skill. Proposed as one atomic group with every paired content win[N] edit and every why rewritten to argue for the side it now sits on. win[4] already read LeBlanc so it needs no edit.

audit.whatIsWrong: The decisive interaction — Miasma grounds Distortion, including the return leg — was in missingInteractions and nowhere on the page. Mirror Image was never mentioned at all, so nothing warned that below 40% health she goes invisible for 1 second and leaves a clone that takes your Twin Fangs for free.
audit.why: Twin Fang is a spammed single-target spell; hosing a damage-less clone with it is the most expensive mistake available in this matchup, and it happens at exactly the moment she is killable.

edits.before: - LeBlanc Distortion: matchup-defining — Dash with a four-second return window — punish the return spot, and remember she is broke after it. Step up only on its downtime. - Budget R Petrifying Gaze for emergencies and the R for opportunities — never swap them.
